objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing package-lock.json routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
required check(s) always fire and gate internally (.github/workflows/tests.yml)
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every pull_request/push workflow (deploy, docs-site, tests) got a deliberate trigger decision and the schedule/issue-driven ones were consciously left alone; critically, the required `unit-tests` check was given the exact working shape — one workflow, no workflow-level path filter, a computed `dorny/paths-filter` output gating the real steps via `if:`, with no companion skip-workflow reporting the same check name.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each filter lists what that workflow actually consumes — deploy's src/package/deploy.sh, docs-site's docs/mkdocs.yml, tests' src/test/package plus each workflow's own file — rather than a catch-all or a copied sibling list.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The agent left nightly-sweep and triage untouched, did not modify the ruleset, and edited only the workflows the audit called for, transparently flagging the one new (necessary and correctly SHA-pinned) third-party action.
